ch_vocab_a1_01.title: Greetings & Basic Expressions
ch_vocab_a1_01.theory:
## Basic Greetings

Let's learn the most common Spanish greetings.

### Time-based Greetings
- **Buenos días** - Good morning (until ~1pm)
- **Buenas tardes** - Good afternoon (until ~8pm)
- **Buenas noches** - Good evening / Good night

### Meeting and Parting
- **¡Hola!** - Hi! (any time of day)
- **¿Qué tal?** / **¿Cómo estás?** - How are you? (informal)
- **¿Cómo está usted?** - How are you? (formal)
- **¡Adiós!** - Goodbye!
- **¡Hasta luego!** - See you later!
- **¡Hasta mañana!** - See you tomorrow!

### Thanks and Apologies
- **Gracias** / **Muchas gracias** - Thank you / Thank you very much
- **De nada** - You're welcome
- **Perdón** / **Disculpe** - Sorry / Excuse me

### Basic Phrases
- **Sí** / **No** - Yes / No
- **Por favor** - Please
- **Lo siento** - I'm sorry
key_points: ¡Hola! can be used at any time of day
Time-based greetings: días (morning), tardes (afternoon), noches (evening)
¿Cómo estás? (informal) vs ¿Cómo está? (formal)
Perdón (minor) vs Lo siento (apology)

vocab_list.example_meaning: Thank you very much for your help.
I'm sorry, I don't speak Spanish.

ch_vocab_a1_02.title: Family & Relationships
ch_vocab_a1_02.theory:
## Family Members

### Immediate Family
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el padre** / **la madre** | father / mother |
| **los padres** | parents |
| **el hijo** / **la hija** | son / daughter |
| **el hermano** / **la hermana** | brother / sister |
| **el esposo** / **la esposa** | husband / wife |

### Extended Family
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el abuelo** / **la abuela** | grandfather / grandmother |
| **el tío** / **la tía** | uncle / aunt |
| **el primo** / **la prima** | cousin (m/f) |
| **el sobrino** / **la sobrina** | nephew / niece |
| **el nieto** / **la nieta** | grandson / granddaughter |

### Relationships
- **el novio** / **la novia** - boyfriend / girlfriend
- **el amigo** / **la amiga** - friend (m/f)
- **el vecino** / **la vecina** - neighbor (m/f)

### Note
All family nouns follow gender patterns: -o (male) / -a (female).
key_points: Family nouns change gender: hermano/hermana, hijo/hija
los padres = parents (not just fathers)
primo/prima = cousin (same word, different gender ending)
el/la are required: el padre, la madre

vocab_list.example: Mi padre trabaja en un banco.
vocab_list.example_meaning: My father works at a bank.

vocab_list.example: Mi abuelo vive en el campo.
vocab_list.example_meaning: My grandfather lives in the countryside.

ch_vocab_a1_03.title: Numbers & Time
ch_vocab_a1_03.theory:
## Telling Time in Spanish

### Asking the Time
- **¿Qué hora es?** - What time is it?

### Answering
- **Es la una.** - It is 1:00. (singular for 1)
- **Son las dos.** - It is 2:00. (plural for 2-12)
- **Son las tres y media.** - It is 3:30.
- **Son las cuatro y cuarto.** - It is 4:15.
- **Son las cinco menos cuarto.** - It is 4:45.

### Time Vocabulary
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **y media** | half past |
| **y cuarto** | quarter past |
| **menos cuarto** | quarter to |
| **en punto** | o'clock (sharp) |
| **de la mañana** | in the morning (AM) |
| **de la tarde** | in the afternoon (PM) |
| **de la noche** | at night (PM) |

### Examples
- Son las ocho **de la mañana**. (It's 8 AM.)
- Son las diez **y diez** de la noche. (It's 10:10 PM.)
key_points: Es la una (singular) vs Son las dos/tres... (plural)
y media (30), y cuarto (15), menos cuarto (45)
de la mañana/tarde/noche for AM/PM
¿A qué hora? = At what time? — A las tres. = At 3:00.

vocab_list.example: Son las tres y diez minutos.

ch_vocab_a1_04.title: Days, Months & Seasons
ch_vocab_a1_04.theory:
## Days of the Week

| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **lunes** | Monday |
| **martes** | Tuesday |
| **miércoles** | Wednesday |
| **jueves** | Thursday |
| **viernes** | Friday |
| **sábado** | Saturday |
| **domingo** | Sunday |

**Note**: Days are NOT capitalized in Spanish. Use **el/los** with days: Trabajo **el lunes**. / No trabajo **los sábados**.

## Months

**enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre**

Months are also NOT capitalized: Mi cumpleaños es en **marzo**.

## Seasons
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **la primavera** | spring |
| **el verano** | summer |
| **el otoño** | autumn/fall |
| **el invierno** | winter |

Use **en** with seasons: **En** verano hace calor.
key_points: Days and months are NOT capitalized in Spanish
Use el/los with days: el lunes (on Monday), los viernes (on Fridays)
Months use 'en': en marzo, en diciembre
Week starts on lunes (Monday) in Spanish-speaking countries

vocab_list.example_meaning: In summer it is very hot.

vocab_list.example: Hay siete días en una semana.
vocab_list.example_meaning: There are seven days in a week.

ch_vocab_a1_05.title: Colors
ch_vocab_a1_05.theory:
## Colors in Spanish

### Colors That Change for Gender
| Masculine | Feminine | English |
|---|---|---|
| **rojo** | **roja** | red |
| **blanco** | **blanca** | white |
| **negro** | **negra** | black |
| **amarillo** | **amarilla** | yellow |

### Colors That Do NOT Change for Gender
These only change for number (add -s/-es for plural):
- **azul** → azules (blue)
- **verde** → verdes (green)
- **gris** → grises (gray)
- **marrón** → marrones (brown)
- **naranja** → naranjas (orange)
- **rosa** → rosas (pink)

### Usage
Colors go **after** the noun:
- Un coche **rojo**. (A red car.)
- Una casa **blanca**. (A white house.)
- Ojos **azules**. (Blue eyes.)

### Asking About Color
- ¿De qué color es? (What color is it?)
- Es **rojo**. / Es **azul**.
key_points: Colors ending in -o change gender: rojo/roja, blanco/blanca
Colors ending in -e or consonant don't change gender: verde, azul, gris
Colors go AFTER the noun: un coche rojo
All colors change for number: rojo→rojos, azul→azules

zumo (Spain) vs jugo (Latin America) for juice

ch_vocab_a1_07.title: Body Parts
ch_vocab_a1_07.theory:
## Parts of the Body

### Head
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **la cabeza** | head |
| **el ojo** | eye |
| **la nariz** | nose |
| **la boca** | mouth |
| **la oreja** | ear |
| **el pelo/cabello** | hair |
| **el diente** | tooth |

### Body
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el brazo** | arm |
| **la mano** | hand |
| **el dedo** | finger |
| **la pierna** | leg |
| **el pie** | foot |
| **la espalda** | back |
| **el estómago** | stomach |
| **el corazón** | heart |

### With Definite Articles (Not Possessives)
Spanish uses **definite articles** instead of possessives for body parts:
- Me duele **la** cabeza. (My head hurts.) — NOT *mi cabeza*
- Levanta **la** mano. (Raise your hand.) — NOT *tu mano*
key_points: la mano is feminine despite ending in -o (exception!)
Use definite articles for body parts: Me duele la cabeza (not mi cabeza)
el dedo = finger OR toe (dedo del pie = toe)
Me duele/duelen for pain: Me duele la cabeza / Me duelen los ojos

ch_vocab_a1_11.title: Professions
ch_vocab_a1_11.theory:
## Common Professions

### Professions with Gender Change (-o/-a)
| Masculine | Feminine | English |
|---|---|---|
| **médico** | **médica** | doctor |
| **abogado** | **abogada** | lawyer |
| **cocinero** | **cocinera** | cook/chef |
| **enfermero** | **enfermera** | nurse |
| **camarero** | **camarera** | waiter/waitress |
| **ingeniero** | **ingeniera** | engineer |

### Professions with Same Form (use el/la)
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el/la periodista** | journalist |
| **el/la dentista** | dentist |
| **el/la artista** | artist |
| **el/la estudiante** | student |
| **el/la policía** | police officer |

### Grammar Rule
No indefinite article with professions after ser:
- Soy **médico**. (I am a doctor.) ✓
- *Soy un médico.* ✗ (incorrect)

BUT with adjectives: Soy **un buen** médico. (I am a good doctor.) ✓
key_points: No article with ser + profession: Soy profesor (not *Soy un profesor*)
Most -o professions change to -a for feminine: médico/médica
Professions ending in -ista don't change: el/la periodista
With adjective, article returns: Es un buen médico

ch_vocab_a1_12.title: Weather & Nature
ch_vocab_a1_12.theory:
## Weather Expressions

Spanish uses different structures for weather:

### Hacer + noun (most common)
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **Hace calor.** | It's hot. |
| **Hace frío.** | It's cold. |
| **Hace sol.** | It's sunny. |
| **Hace viento.** | It's windy. |
| **Hace buen/mal tiempo.** | The weather is good/bad. |

### Verb alone
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **Llueve.** (llover) | It rains. / It's raining. |
| **Nieva.** (nevar) | It snows. / It's snowing. |

### Estar/Hay
- **Está nublado.** - It's cloudy.
- **Hay niebla.** - It's foggy.
- **Hay tormenta.** - There's a storm.

## Nature Vocabulary
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el sol** | sun |
| **la luna** | moon |
| **el mar** | sea |
| **el río** | river |
| **la montaña** | mountain |
| **el bosque** | forest |
| **el árbol** | tree |
| **la flor** | flower |
key_points: Hace + noun: Hace calor/frío/sol/viento
Llueve/Nieva are used alone (no 'hace')
Está nublado, Hay niebla — different structures
¿Qué tiempo hace? = How's the weather?

vocab_list.example: Hay muchos árboles en el parque.
vocab_list.example_meaning: There are many trees in the park.

ch_vocab_a1_13.title: Transportation
ch_vocab_a1_13.theory:
## Means of Transportation

| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **el coche/carro** | car |
| **el autobús/bus** | bus |
| **el tren** | train |
| **el avión** | airplane |
| **el metro** | subway/metro |

| **el taxi** | taxi |
| **el barco** | boat/ship |
| **la moto(cicleta)** | motorcycle |
| **a pie** | on foot |

### Prepositions with Transport
- **en** coche/bus/tren/avión/metro/taxi/barco/bici/moto
- **a** pie (on foot — exception!)

### Useful Phrases
- **Voy en autobús.** - I go by bus.
- **Vamos a pie.** - We go on foot.
- **¿Cómo vas al trabajo?** - How do you go to work?

### Note
- **coche** (Spain) vs **carro** (Latin America) for car
- **autobús** (Spain) vs **bus/colectivo/camión** (Latin America)
key_points: en + transport: en coche, en tren, en avión
Exception: a pie (on foot), NOT en pie
coche (Spain) vs carro (Latin America)
Tomar/coger el bus/metro = to take the bus/metro

vocab_list.example_meaning: I go to work by car.

vocab_list.example: El tren llega a las diez.
Voy a la escuela en bicicleta.

ch_vocab_a1_14.title: Daily Verbs
ch_vocab_a1_14.theory:
## Essential Daily Verbs

### Daily Routine
| Spanish | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **levantarse** | to get up | Me levanto a las siete. |
| **desayunar** | to have breakfast | Desayuno a las ocho. |
| **ducharse** | to shower | Me ducho por la mañana. |
| **vestirse** | to get dressed | Me visto rápido. |
| **almorzar** | to have lunch | Almuerzo a la una. |
| **cenar** | to have dinner | Cenamos a las nueve. |
| **acostarse** | to go to bed | Me acuesto a las once. |
| **dormir** | to sleep | Duermo ocho horas. |

### Common Actions
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **hacer** | to do/make |
| **leer** | to read |
| **ver** | to see/watch |
| **escuchar** | to listen |
| **llamar** | to call |
| **esperar** | to wait |
| **abrir** | to open |
| **cerrar** | to close |

### Note
Reflexive verbs (levantarse, ducharse, vestirse, acostarse) use reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nos, os, se.
key_points: Reflexive verbs for daily routine: levantarse, ducharse, acostarse
desayunar/almorzar/cenar = breakfast/lunch/dinner (no reflexive needed)
hacer = to do/make (very versatile: hacer la cama, hacer deporte)
Common pattern: Me levanto, me ducho, desayuno, trabajo...

ch_vocab_a1_15.title: Emotions & States
ch_vocab_a1_15.theory:
## Emotions and States

Emotions and states use **estar** (not ser):

### Common Emotions
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **contento/a** | happy/content |
| **triste** | sad |
| **enfadado/a** / **enojado/a** | angry |
| **nervioso/a** | nervous |
| **preocupado/a** | worried |
| **sorprendido/a** | surprised |
| **asustado/a** | scared |
| **aburrido/a** | bored |
| **emocionado/a** | excited |

### Physical States
| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| **cansado/a** | tired |
| **enfermo/a** | sick |
| **bien** | well/fine |
| **mal** | bad/unwell |
| **ocupado/a** | busy |

### Usage
- **Estoy** contento. (I am happy.) — temporary emotion, uses **estar**
- ¿Cómo **estás**? — **Estoy** bien, gracias. (How are you? — I'm fine, thanks.)

### Ser vs Estar with Emotions
- **Estar** triste = to be sad (right now)
- **Ser** triste = to be a sad person (personality trait)
key_points: Emotions use ESTAR (temporary states): Estoy contento
enfadado (Spain) vs enojado (Latin America) for angry
Adjective must agree in gender: contento/contenta, cansado/cansada
Ser triste (sad person) vs Estar triste (feeling sad now)
